issue: Test suite produced intermittent FileNotFoundError failures under pytest on macOS when run in rapid succession, caused by two independent but interacting bugs: (1) per-test tmpdir creation on macOS APFS is subject to daemon-driven eviction between test methods, and (2) a builtins.open mock in a daemon thread was never cleaned up on timeout, corrupting the module loader for all subsequent tests in the session.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE 1 (test code): Each test class setUp() called tempfile.mkdtemp() to create a fresh directory per test method. On macOS, /var/folders entries are managed by the APFS daemon and can be evicted between calls; with rapid back-to-back test methods the path returned by a previous mkdtemp() could disappear before the next setUp() completed its os.makedirs-equivalent, producing FileNotFoundError inside importlib. ROOT CAUSE 2 (production code): benchmark/ground_truth/validator.py _run_single() wrapped execution in a unittest.mock.patch('builtins.open', mock_open()) context manager inside a daemon thread. When the thread timed out (e.g. the time.sleep(60) test), the thread was abandoned and context manager __exit__ was never called, leaving builtins.open globally patched to return empty data. Subsequent calls to importlib's spec.loader.exec_module() internally call open() to read .py source files; with open() mocked to return empty content, exec_module produced empty module objects. On the next setUp(), the stale tmpdir from root cause 1 was gone and importlib's internal get_data() raised FileNotFoundError, producing cascading failures across the rest of the session.
fix_summary: Two-part fix: (1) replaced per-test tempfile.mkdtemp() with a single session-level _SESSION_TMPDIR created at module import time, with _make_test_dir() returning unique subdirectories under it — the parent dir is guaranteed to persist for the entire process lifetime and is removed via atexit; (2) replaced the mock.patch('builtins.open', mock_open()) context manager in _run_single() with direct sys.stdout reassignment using try/finally, which guarantees stdout cleanup even when a daemon thread is abandoned on timeout, eliminating the global mock leak.

fix_details.change_1: benchmark/ground_truth/test_validator.py: Added module-level _SESSION_TMPDIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='sbg_gt_tests_') at import time, registered _shutil.rmtree cleanup via atexit, and added _make_test_dir() which increments a counter and creates a unique subdirectory under _SESSION_TMPDIR. All 12 setUp() methods that previously called tempfile.mkdtemp() now call _make_test_dir() instead.
fix_details.change_2: benchmark/ground_truth/validator.py _run_single(): Removed the unittest.mock.patch('builtins.open', mock_open()) context manager that wrapped program execution inside the daemon thread. Replaced with direct sys.stdout = buf assignment guarded by a try/finally block that restores sys.stdout = old_stdout, ensuring cleanup on both normal return and thread abandonment due to timeout.

production_change_justification: validator.py was modified to remove the builtins.open mock from _run_single(). This is a behavioral change: programs under test that call open() now receive FileNotFoundError (or whatever the real filesystem returns) rather than mock empty data. This is strictly more correct for SBG's purposes — the validator is meant to test actual program behavior, and silently feeding mock data to open() calls was masking real program semantics. The fix also closes a cross-thread global state leak that made the entire test session non-deterministic after any timeout.
regression_risk: LOW - fix narrows mock scope, does not alter behavioral semantics
